subject: Staged reservation phasing + KPI alignment — dedicated GPU mix and tail budget
messages:
From: Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@acmehealth.com>

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Apr 2027 14:32:00 -0000
Subject: Request: staged reservation phasing + throughput targets for pilot->prod

Laura / Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. ApexTech is planning a phased commitment for dedicated inference. We're targeting a pilot (months 0–3) serving 40k inference requests/day peaking at ~250 concurrent sessions, then ramping to steady-state prod (months 4–12) at ~450k requests/day. Key constraints: 95th-percentile generation latency target of <=220ms for conversational flows, and a strict tail budget for ad‑hoc analytic embedding jobs.

Can you share a suggested phasing plan that shows:
- GPU family mix we should reserve (A100 vs H100 vs potential L40s for embeddings)
- Slotting plan across a reserved pool (how many slots per tier)
- Expected throughput (tokens/s) per node for the suggested models (we'll likely run a 13B chat model + a 4B embedding transformer)
- How burst capacity will be handled and what costs are exposed if we rely on burst lanes

I've attached our current internal workbook (ApexTech_reservation_workbook_v2.xlsx) with traffic curves and a list of peak windows. We need a draft recommendation and a rough cost delta by EOD Thursday so the procurement team can review.

Thanks — Ethan
Ethan Rogers
Head of AI Platform, ApexTech

Attachments: ApexTech_reservation_workbook_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: staged reservation phasing + throughput targets for pilot->prod

Ethan —

Appreciate the clear traffic curves. Quick high-level reply while Karthik and Ben populate numbers from our load bench:

1) Phasing: we recommend a three-phase approach — Pilot (0–3m), Ramp (4–6m), Steady (7–12m). Pilot uses smaller pod counts with H100 for latency-sensitive chat; Ramp introduces a mixed pool adding A100s for cost-effective batch handling; Steady moves to a blended pool tuned for MLQ (mixed precision) to lower unit cost.

2) Slotting: suggest reserving two priority lanes for low-latency chat (H100 family) and a larger general-purpose lane (A100) for embeddings and batch generation. We can show an explicit slot-to-VM mapping in the workbook.

3) Burst: burst lanes can be guaranteed up to X% of committed capacity (we'll quantify). We'll include modeled examples showing cost if burst usage exceeds the committed threshold.

Ben / Karthik — can you take the workbook and return a table with: GPU family, nodes required per phase, estimated tokens/s per node (chat 13B, embed 4B), expected 95th latency, and an estimated monthly committed cost + burst delta?

Ethan — will loop back with the draft workbook and one-slide SLA exception summary (tail budget) by EOD Thu.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Apr 2027 03:25:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: staged reservation phasing + throughput targets for pilot->prod

Quick technical notes (bench numbers attached in-sheet):

- 13B chat model (FP16, KV cache warm): H100-80GB: ~1.2k tokens/s per GPU for conversational streams when batched to 32; A100-40GB: ~700 tokens/s under similar batching. Tail latency at 95th in pilot (low batch) is ~180–240ms on single H100 depending on request size.

- 4B embedding model (quantized INT8 candidate): L40s or A100 are cost-effective — L40s give good price/perf for high-concurrency embedding workloads (approx 2.6k embeddings/s per card).

- Recommendation: Pilot (2x H100 + 1x A100) to keep latency SLO conservative. Ramp: add 6x A100s and 2x H100s; Steady: scale to blended pool (8x A100, 4x H100) with autoscale headroom. We'll include expected p99 tail multipliers and a slotting sketch.

I'll populate the tokens/s and a cost delta using current MSRP and our internal committed-rate estimates; attaching a short bench table (embedded into the workbook)

— Karthik
